title: English
description: ISC Class XI English: Paper 1 (English Language, 3 hours, 80 marks) and Paper 2 (Literature in English, 3 hours, 80 marks), plus internal assessment in speaking/listening.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 Regulations and Syllabuses - English (www.cisce.org).
syllabusBaselines.note: Verified October 2026. Paper 1: language skills, comprehension, composition. Paper 2: drama, prose and poetry from prescribed texts.

sections.title: English Language (Paper 1)
sections.description: Composition, directed writing, grammar and comprehension skills.

chapters.title: Composition
chapters.blurb: Planning, organising and drafting descriptive, narrative, argumentative and reflective pieces of writing.

chapters.title: Directed Writing
chapters.blurb: Proposals, reports, speeches, articles and formal/informal letters to a given brief.

chapters.title: Grammar and Usage
chapters.blurb: Tense consistency, sentence structure, punctuation, agreement, conciseness and error correction.

chapters.title: Comprehension
chapters.blurb: Unseen passages with inference, vocabulary in context and summary writing.

chapters.title: Literary Devices and Close Reading
chapters.blurb: Imagery, tone, figurative language, structure and dramatic methods applied to unseen and set texts.

chapters.title: Macbeth — Acts I and II
chapters.blurb: Shakespeare's Macbeth (Acts I & II): the witches' predictions, the pressure of ambition, and the immediate psychological cost of the murder of Duncan. Prescribed for Class XI only.

chapters.title: A Living God
chapters.blurb: Lafcadio Hearn's short story about a reluctant priest and the strange meaning of a small stone idol in a village's faith. Prescribed in PRISM: A Collection of ISC Short Stories.

chapters.title: Advice to Youth
chapters.blurb: Mark Twain's satirical piece of 'advice' to young people about manners, morals and the gap between adult instruction and adult behaviour. Prescribed in PRISM: A Collection of ISC Short Stories.

chapters.title: The Paper Menagerie
chapters.blurb: Ken Liu's story of a boy, his mother's origami animals and the loss that comes from rejecting the language and culture of home. Prescribed in PRISM: A Collection of ISC Short Stories.

chapters.title: The Great Automatic Grammatizator
chapters.blurb: Roald Dahl's fable about a machine that can write stories and the fear of becoming unnecessary to one's own craft. Prescribed in PRISM: A Collection of ISC Short Stories.

chapters.title: Thank You, Ma'am
chapters.blurb: Langston Hughes's short story of a failed theft, an unexpected act of trust and the brief encounter that changes how a boy sees himself. Prescribed in PRISM: A Collection of ISC Short Stories.

chapters.title: Abhisara: The Tryst
chapters.blurb: Rabindranath Tagore's poem of waiting, a delayed meeting and the uneasy question of whether anything was fully understood. Prescribed in RHAPSODY: A Collection of ISC Poems.

chapters.title: Why I Like the Hospital
chapters.blurb: Tony Hoagland's darkly comic poem about a place that makes private pain socially acceptable to show. Prescribed in RHAPSODY: A Collection of ISC Poems.

chapters.title: Sonnet 116
chapters.blurb: Shakespeare's sonnet defining ideal love as constant, unshaken by change, time or difficulty. Prescribed in RHAPSODY: A Collection of ISC Poems.

chapters.title: Death of a Naturalist
chapters.blurb: Seamus Heaney's poem about a childhood fascination with frogs giving way to fear and the end of a tender way of seeing nature. Prescribed in RHAPSODY: A Collection of ISC Poems.

chapters.title: Strange Meeting
chapters.blurb: Wilfred Owen's poem of a meeting between enemies in a strange underworld and the deep waste and sorrow of war. Prescribed in RHAPSODY: A Collection of ISC Poems.
